def check_n(n, k_max=100):
    # We want to see if there exists a sequence a_k such that
    # a_{k-1} = k * (a_k - k**(n-1))
    # This means a_0 = k! * a_k - sum_{j=1}^k (k!/j!) * j**(n-1)
    # Let T_k = sum_{j=1}^k (k!/j!) * j**(n-1)
    # Then a_0 = k! * a_k - T_k
    # So a_0 \equiv -T_k (mod k!)
    
    # Let's compute x_k = -T_k % k!
    x = [0] * (k_max + 1)
    T = 0
    fact = 1
    for k in range(1, k_max + 1):
        fact *= k
        # T_k = k * T_{k-1} + k**(n-1) * (k!/k!) = k * T_{k-1} + k**(n-1)
        # This is not right. T_k = sum_{j=1}^k (k!/j!) * j**(n-1)
        # T_1 = 1!/1! * 1**(n-1) = 1
        # T_2 = 2!/1! * 1**(n-1) + 2!/2! * 2**(n-1) = 2 * 1 + 2**(n-1)
        # T_k = k * T_{k-1} + k**(n-1)
        if k == 1:
            T = 1
        else:
            T = k * T + k**(n-1)
        
        x[k] = (-T) % fact
    return x

for n in range(1, 7):
    print(f"n={n}: {check_n(n, 10)[:10]}")
